**Docusign, Inc.** is an American software company headquartered in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") that provides products for organizations to manage electronic agreements and contract lifecycle processes with [electronic signatures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_signature "Electronic signature") and AI supported data extraction on different devices.

In April 2018, Docusign filed for an [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering"). At the time of the IPO, the largest shareholders were venture investment firms Sigma Partners, Ignition Partners, Frazier Technology Ventures, and former CEO [Keith Krach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_J._Krach "Keith J. Krach") was the largest individual shareholder. None of the original founders are major shareholders.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-ipoinvestors-6) The company went public on the [Nasdaq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasdaq "Nasdaq") on April 27, 2018.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-7)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Docusign&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Docusign was founded in 2003 by Court Lorenzini, Tom Gonser, and Eric Ranft.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-8) Tom Gonser came up with the idea when he was [CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEO "CEO") of NetUpdate, a company he founded in 1998. Throughout its history, NetUpdate had acquired several companies, including an e-signature start-up in Seattle called DocuTouch, funded by Timberline Venture Partners, Bill Kallman, and Jeff Tung with $4M. Timberline invested another $1 million in the merger into NetUpdate.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-DocGon-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-NetUp-10) DocuTouch held patents on Web-based digital signatures and collaboration. With internal support from Gonser, Lorenzini negotiated the purchase of certain DocuTouch assets from NetUpdate and started Docusign. Gonser then left the NetUpdate Board to focus on Docusign full-time.

The firm began sales in 2005 when zipForm, now zipLogix, integrated Docusign into its virtual real estate forms. According to Docusign, mock trials featuring licensed attorneys and judges highlighted the admissibility of Docusign contracts in court based on encrypted audit logs of signature events, and the impossibility of changing contracts.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Mock-11)

In January 2007, Court Lorenzini stepped down as CEO and board chairman and was replaced as CEO by Matthew Schiltz,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-12) who served in that role until January 2010.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-:1-13) Steven King replaced Schultz as CEO[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-:1-13) and moved the corporate headquarters from Seattle to San Francisco. [Keith Krach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Krach "Keith Krach") became Docusign's board chairman in January 2010 and its CEO in August 2011.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-14)

Docusign began referring to its service as "eSignature Transaction Management". By the end of 2010, the company had handled 73 percent of the [SaaS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_as_a_service "Software as a service")-based electronic signature market, with 80 million signatures processed.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-80Mil-15)[Scale Venture Partners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scale_Venture_Partners "Scale Venture Partners") led an investment round of $27 million in December 2010.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Scale-16)

Docusign opened an office in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England"), in September 2011.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-London-17) In the same year, Docusign opened an office in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco") that now functions as its global headquarters.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-18)

Docusign signed an agreement with [PayPal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PayPal "PayPal") in April 2012 that allowed users to capture signatures and payments in a single transaction.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-PayPal-19) Similar partnerships with [Salesforce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salesforce "Salesforce")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Salesforce-20) and [Google Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Drive "Google Drive")[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Google-21) preceded the [PayPal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PayPal "PayPal") agreement.

On January 10, 2013, Docusign and [Equifax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equifax "Equifax") announced a partnership to simplify electronic delivery of the Requests for Transcript of Tax Return Form 4506-T to the United States [Internal Revenue Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_Revenue_Service "Internal Revenue Service"). Under the partnership, Equifax allows lenders to use Docusign to securely send requests to loan applicants. Docusign and[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-22) Equifax were among 14 firms that participated in a nine-month feasibility study of electronic signatures for 4506-T forms in 2011.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Equifax-23)

In October 2015, [Keith Krach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Krach "Keith Krach") announced he would step down as CEO once a search for a new CEO was completed.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-24)

In January 2017, veteran [software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software "Software")[executive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_management "Senior management") Daniel Springer was named the new CEO.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-26)

Docusign ranked number 6 on [Fast Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Company "Fast Company")'s Most Innovative Enterprise Tech Companies of 2022, with an overall market share of 61%.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-27)

On June 21, 2022, Daniel Springer was replaced as CEO by Mary Agnes "Maggie" Wilderotter,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-28) and later Allan Thygesen as CEO on September 22, 2022. Thygesen assumed office on October 10.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-29)

In April 2024, the company announced a significant expansion of its company strategy, opening up a new SaaS category — Intelligent Agreement Management — and launching Docusign IAM, an Intelligent Agreement Management platform and new line-of-business-focused applications to lead that category.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-31)

### Funding

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Docusign&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Funding")]

In 2004, Docusign raised $4.6 million from Ignition Partners and Frazier Technology Ventures.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Frazier-32) In 2006, Sigma Partners became the largest shareholder, a position it held at the time of the IPO, with returns over $700 million.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Sigma-33) Between 2006 and 2009 Docusign raised $30 million that allowed the firm to add corporate clients and process 48 million signatures.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-34)

In July 2012, Docusign raised $47.5 million in venture funding from investors including [Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kleiner_Perkins_Caufield_&_Byers "Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers"); the round later grew closer to $56 million.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Kleiner-36) In March 2014, the company announced it had raised $85 million in a new funding round.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-37) Though unconfirmed, _[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wall\_Street\_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")_ reported the round was based on a company valuation of $1.6 billion.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-38)

In May 2015, the company announced it had raised $233 million in a new funding round, with some estimating a $3 billion company valuation.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-40)

In 2018, the company announced plans for an [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") on the [Nasdaq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasdaq "Nasdaq").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-41) The IPO was completed on April 27, in which the company raised $543 million. Neither the original founders nor CEO Daniel Springer were major shareholders at that time.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-42) Former CEO Keith Krach was the largest individual shareholder at 5.5%, about 8.5 million shares at the time of the IPO. Venture capital firms Sigma Partners, Ignition Partners, and now-defunct company Frazier Technology Ventures were the largest non-individual shareholders.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-ipoinvestors-6)

## Acquisitions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Docusign&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Acquisitions")]

In May 2013, Docusign acquired Cartavi, a Naperville-based startup that made real estate software.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-43) This was later converted into Docusign Rooms and the base API for Docusign Workspaces.

In July 2018, Docusign acquired [SpringCM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpringCM "SpringCM") for $220 million.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-45)

In February 2020, Docusign acquired Seal Software for $188 million.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-47)

On June 1, 2021, DocuSign acquired Clause, a legal contract technology startup.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-49)

In May 2024 the company acquired Lexion, an AI contract management company, for a reported $165 million.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-51)

## Products

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Docusign&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Products")]

Docusign's services are offered either by subscription or through a [mobile app](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_app "Mobile app"). Docusign released the mobile app in November 2011.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Digital-52)

Docusign Professional emails recipients an electronically signed document requesting review of a document after it is uploaded. Each party must agree to complete business electronically, review the document, and apply a signature. Signatures may be added from a stored copy of a signature or generated automatically by the software. Phone confirmation and background checks are offered as premium services.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-DocuSign-53)

## Litigation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Docusign&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Litigation")]

In a 2016 case, it was found that a lawyer in Sacramento who had exclusively been using Docusign signatures had the signatures rendered invalid due to the legal requirements of a physical signature known as a [wet signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signature#Wet_signatures "Signature").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-54)

A [class action lawsuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_action "Class action") began against Docusign in 2022 regarding their conduct from 2020-2021 that alleged the company misled investors and shareholders with false reporting. According to the initial complaint, Docusign "failed to disclose the role the COVID-19 pandemic had on its growth, including the positive impact on Docusign's business. [Docusign] also downplayed the impact that a 'return to normal' would have on the Company's growth and business."[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-56)

In 2023, the company's former CEO Daniel Springer filed a lawsuit against Docusign. While the company claimed that Springer had resigned, his lawsuit alleged that the resignation was fabricated.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-57)

**Docusign, Inc.** is an American software company headquartered in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") that provides products for organizations to manage electronic agreements and contract lifecycle processes with [electronic signatures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_signature "Electronic signature") and AI supported data extraction on different devices.

In April 2018, Docusign filed for an [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering"). At the time of the IPO, the largest shareholders were venture investment firms Sigma Partners, Ignition Partners, Frazier Technology Ventures, and former CEO [Keith Krach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_J._Krach "Keith J. Krach") was the largest individual shareholder. None of the original founders are major shareholders.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-ipoinvestors-6) The company went public on the [Nasdaq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasdaq "Nasdaq") on April 27, 2018.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-7)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Docusign&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Docusign was founded in 2003 by Court Lorenzini, Tom Gonser, and Eric Ranft.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-8) Tom Gonser came up with the idea when he was [CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEO "CEO") of NetUpdate, a company he founded in 1998. Throughout its history, NetUpdate had acquired several companies, including an e-signature start-up in Seattle called DocuTouch, funded by Timberline Venture Partners, Bill Kallman, and Jeff Tung with $4M. Timberline invested another $1 million in the merger into NetUpdate.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-DocGon-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-NetUp-10) DocuTouch held patents on Web-based digital signatures and collaboration. With internal support from Gonser, Lorenzini negotiated the purchase of certain DocuTouch assets from NetUpdate and started Docusign. Gonser then left the NetUpdate Board to focus on Docusign full-time.

The firm began sales in 2005 when zipForm, now zipLogix, integrated Docusign into its virtual real estate forms. According to Docusign, mock trials featuring licensed attorneys and judges highlighted the admissibility of Docusign contracts in court based on encrypted audit logs of signature events, and the impossibility of changing contracts.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Mock-11)

In January 2007, Court Lorenzini stepped down as CEO and board chairman and was replaced as CEO by Matthew Schiltz,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-12) who served in that role until January 2010.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-:1-13) Steven King replaced Schultz as CEO[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-:1-13) and moved the corporate headquarters from Seattle to San Francisco. [Keith Krach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Krach "Keith Krach") became Docusign's board chairman in January 2010 and its CEO in August 2011.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-14)

Docusign began referring to its service as "eSignature Transaction Management". By the end of 2010, the company had handled 73 percent of the [SaaS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_as_a_service "Software as a service")-based electronic signature market, with 80 million signatures processed.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-80Mil-15)[Scale Venture Partners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scale_Venture_Partners "Scale Venture Partners") led an investment round of $27 million in December 2010.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Scale-16)

Docusign opened an office in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England"), in September 2011.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-London-17) In the same year, Docusign opened an office in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco") that now functions as its global headquarters.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-18)

Docusign signed an agreement with [PayPal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PayPal "PayPal") in April 2012 that allowed users to capture signatures and payments in a single transaction.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-PayPal-19) Similar partnerships with [Salesforce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salesforce "Salesforce")[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Salesforce-20) and [Google Drive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Drive "Google Drive")[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Google-21) preceded the [PayPal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PayPal "PayPal") agreement.

On January 10, 2013, Docusign and [Equifax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equifax "Equifax") announced a partnership to simplify electronic delivery of the Requests for Transcript of Tax Return Form 4506-T to the United States [Internal Revenue Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_Revenue_Service "Internal Revenue Service"). Under the partnership, Equifax allows lenders to use Docusign to securely send requests to loan applicants. Docusign and[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-22) Equifax were among 14 firms that participated in a nine-month feasibility study of electronic signatures for 4506-T forms in 2011.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Equifax-23)

In October 2015, [Keith Krach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Krach "Keith Krach") announced he would step down as CEO once a search for a new CEO was completed.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-24)

In January 2017, veteran [software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software "Software")[executive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senior_management "Senior management") Daniel Springer was named the new CEO.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-26)

Docusign ranked number 6 on [Fast Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Company "Fast Company")'s Most Innovative Enterprise Tech Companies of 2022, with an overall market share of 61%.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-27)

On June 21, 2022, Daniel Springer was replaced as CEO by Mary Agnes "Maggie" Wilderotter,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-28) and later Allan Thygesen as CEO on September 22, 2022. Thygesen assumed office on October 10.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-29)

In April 2024, the company announced a significant expansion of its company strategy, opening up a new SaaS category — Intelligent Agreement Management — and launching Docusign IAM, an Intelligent Agreement Management platform and new line-of-business-focused applications to lead that category.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-31)

### Funding

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Docusign&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Funding")]

In 2004, Docusign raised $4.6 million from Ignition Partners and Frazier Technology Ventures.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Frazier-32) In 2006, Sigma Partners became the largest shareholder, a position it held at the time of the IPO, with returns over $700 million.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Sigma-33) Between 2006 and 2009 Docusign raised $30 million that allowed the firm to add corporate clients and process 48 million signatures.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-34)

In July 2012, Docusign raised $47.5 million in venture funding from investors including [Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kleiner_Perkins_Caufield_&_Byers "Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers"); the round later grew closer to $56 million.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Kleiner-36) In March 2014, the company announced it had raised $85 million in a new funding round.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-37) Though unconfirmed, _[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wall\_Street\_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")_ reported the round was based on a company valuation of $1.6 billion.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-38)

In May 2015, the company announced it had raised $233 million in a new funding round, with some estimating a $3 billion company valuation.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-40)

In 2018, the company announced plans for an [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") on the [Nasdaq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasdaq "Nasdaq").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-41) The IPO was completed on April 27, in which the company raised $543 million. Neither the original founders nor CEO Daniel Springer were major shareholders at that time.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-42) Former CEO Keith Krach was the largest individual shareholder at 5.5%, about 8.5 million shares at the time of the IPO. Venture capital firms Sigma Partners, Ignition Partners, and now-defunct company Frazier Technology Ventures were the largest non-individual shareholders.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-ipoinvestors-6)

## Acquisitions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Docusign&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Acquisitions")]

In May 2013, Docusign acquired Cartavi, a Naperville-based startup that made real estate software.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-43) This was later converted into Docusign Rooms and the base API for Docusign Workspaces.

In July 2018, Docusign acquired [SpringCM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpringCM "SpringCM") for $220 million.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-45)

In February 2020, Docusign acquired Seal Software for $188 million.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-47)

On June 1, 2021, DocuSign acquired Clause, a legal contract technology startup.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-49)

In May 2024 the company acquired Lexion, an AI contract management company, for a reported $165 million.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-51)

## Products

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Docusign&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Products")]

Docusign's services are offered either by subscription or through a [mobile app](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_app "Mobile app"). Docusign released the mobile app in November 2011.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-Digital-52)

Docusign Professional emails recipients an electronically signed document requesting review of a document after it is uploaded. Each party must agree to complete business electronically, review the document, and apply a signature. Signatures may be added from a stored copy of a signature or generated automatically by the software. Phone confirmation and background checks are offered as premium services.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-DocuSign-53)

## Litigation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Docusign&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Litigation")]

In a 2016 case, it was found that a lawyer in Sacramento who had exclusively been using Docusign signatures had the signatures rendered invalid due to the legal requirements of a physical signature known as a [wet signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signature#Wet_signatures "Signature").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-54)

A [class action lawsuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_action "Class action") began against Docusign in 2022 regarding their conduct from 2020-2021 that alleged the company misled investors and shareholders with false reporting. According to the initial complaint, Docusign "failed to disclose the role the COVID-19 pandemic had on its growth, including the positive impact on Docusign's business. [Docusign] also downplayed the impact that a 'return to normal' would have on the Company's growth and business."[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-56)

In 2023, the company's former CEO Daniel Springer filed a lawsuit against Docusign. While the company claimed that Springer had resigned, his lawsuit alleged that the resignation was fabricated.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DocuSign#cite_note-57)

**ACI Worldwide** is a digital payments software company headquartered in [Elkhorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elkhorn,_Omaha,_Nebraska "Elkhorn, Omaha, Nebraska"), [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska"), that processes billions of transactions daily equating to trillions of U.S. dollars for customers in 94 countries.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-2) Banks, financial institutions, merchants, billers, acquirers, issuers, and other third-party payment service providers use its intelligent solutions to deploy secure payment rails across all channels.

## Partnerships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ACI_Worldwide&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Partnerships")]

ACI Worldwide has partnered with organizations like [AWS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Web_Services "Amazon Web Services"), [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google"), [Red Hat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Hat "Red Hat"), [IBM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM "IBM"), [Mastercard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastercard "Mastercard"), [Visa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_Inc. "Visa Inc."), and other [fintech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_technology "Financial technology") innovators to enable banks, merchants, and billers to easily and securely accept, transform, and transmit any payment instantly on a platform.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ACI_Worldwide&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

ACI was founded in [Omaha, Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omaha,_Nebraska "Omaha, Nebraska") as **A**pplied **C**ommunications **I**nc, on September 1, 1975, to develop software for communications applications using the new [NonStop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NonStop_(server_computers) "NonStop (server computers)") computers from [Tandem Computers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tandem_Computers "Tandem Computers"). The founders were James Cody, Dave Willadsen, and Dennis Gates. Chuck Hackett, Charly Foglesong, and Mike May began ACI's relationship with Tandem. Early projects involved building systems to handle [ATMs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_teller_machine "Automated teller machine") and front ends for [core banking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Core_banking "Core banking") systems, which led to the launch of the first product, [BASE24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BASE24 "BASE24"), in 1982. BASE24 was coined by a salesman to represent "Baseline Software for 24 hour-per-day system operations".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-3)

BASE24 was expanded over time to service transactions from other channels, such as [POS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/POS_terminal "POS terminal") terminals and bank branch systems. The product portfolio grew to cover functions related to card transactions, such as clearing, settlement and [fraud detection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud_detection "Fraud detection"). The hardware support for these products was extended to suppliers [IBM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM "IBM"), [HP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hewlett-Packard "Hewlett-Packard"), [Stratus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratus_Technologies "Stratus Technologies") and [Sun Microsystems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Microsystems "Sun Microsystems").

In the 1990s, ACI's product range was expanded to cover [wholesale banking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wholesale_banking "Wholesale banking") payments with software for [ACH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_Clearing_House "Automated Clearing House") transactions and [wire transfers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wire_transfer "Wire transfer") leading to the acquisition of IntraNet, Inc. in 1998,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-4) and adding the Money Transfer System product.

Since 1995, ACI has been publicly traded on [NASDAQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASDAQ "NASDAQ"), initially under the name Transaction Systems Architects (TSA), and, since July 2007, under the name ACI Worldwide, Inc. (ACIW).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-ACI-5) Prior to that ACI had periods of ownership by [US West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_West "US West") and Tandem, and as a private company.

### Acquisitions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ACI_Worldwide&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Acquisitions")]

*   1998: IntraNet, Inc.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-6) was acquired by ACI Worldwide's predecessor Transaction Systems Architects, Inc. IntraNet, Inc. manufactured software systems to facilitate electronic payments.
*   2005: S2 Systems signed an agreement to sell substantially all its assets to Transaction Systems Architects, Inc.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-7)
*   2005: Restructuring of Transaction Systems Architects, Inc. into a highly focused organization, merging ACI, Insession, and IntraNet [[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-9) into one operating unit under the name ACI Worldwide. The name change became official in July 2007.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-ACI-5)
*   2006: P&H Solutions Inc., a provider of a Web-based corporate cash management product, was acquired by ACI Worldwide.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-10)
*   2006: Electronic Payment Systems AG (eps) was acquired.
*   2007: Stratasoft Sdn Bhd was acquired.
*   2007: Visual WEB Solutions Inc.,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-11) a financial banking applications company, was acquired.
*   2009: Euronet Essentis[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-12) was purchased by ACI to expand card issuing and merchant management capabilities[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-13)
*   2011: The acquisition of ISD Corporation was announced[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-14) to broaden the functionality of ACI's payments products for retailers.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-15)
*   2012: [S1 Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S1_Corporation "S1 Corporation") was acquired[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-16) to broaden ACI's suite of payment offerings for financial organizations, processors and retailers.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-18)
*   2012: North Data Uruguay S.A. was acquired.
*   2012: Distra Pty Ltd was acquired.
*   2013: Online Resources Corporation was acquired.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-19)
*   2013: Official Payments Holdings,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-20) a provider of electronic bill payment technology, was acquired. The company processed approximately 20 million payments, totaling over $9 billion annually.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-ACI_Worldwide,_Inc._Form_10-K_Period_Ending_December_31,_2013-21)
*   2013: Profesionales en Transacciones Electronicas S.A. (PTESA) was acquired.
*   2014: An agreement to acquire Retail Decisions (ReD) was announced[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-23) and completed on August 12, 2014.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-24)
*   2015: PAY.ON, which provides white-label hosted payment gateway services, was acquired.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-25)
*   2019: ACI enters agreement to acquire Speedpay,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-26) Western Union's U.S. bill pay business, for $750 million [[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-27)
*   2019: Walletron was acquired.

**ACI Worldwide** is a digital payments software company headquartered in [Elkhorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elkhorn,_Omaha,_Nebraska "Elkhorn, Omaha, Nebraska"), [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska"), that processes billions of transactions daily equating to trillions of U.S. dollars for customers in 94 countries.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-2) Banks, financial institutions, merchants, billers, acquirers, issuers, and other third-party payment service providers use its intelligent solutions to deploy secure payment rails across all channels.

## Partnerships

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ACI_Worldwide&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Partnerships")]

ACI Worldwide has partnered with organizations like [AWS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Web_Services "Amazon Web Services"), [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google"), [Red Hat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Hat "Red Hat"), [IBM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM "IBM"), [Mastercard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastercard "Mastercard"), [Visa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_Inc. "Visa Inc."), and other [fintech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_technology "Financial technology") innovators to enable banks, merchants, and billers to easily and securely accept, transform, and transmit any payment instantly on a platform.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ACI_Worldwide&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

ACI was founded in [Omaha, Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omaha,_Nebraska "Omaha, Nebraska") as **A**pplied **C**ommunications **I**nc, on September 1, 1975, to develop software for communications applications using the new [NonStop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NonStop_(server_computers) "NonStop (server computers)") computers from [Tandem Computers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tandem_Computers "Tandem Computers"). The founders were James Cody, Dave Willadsen, and Dennis Gates. Chuck Hackett, Charly Foglesong, and Mike May began ACI's relationship with Tandem. Early projects involved building systems to handle [ATMs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_teller_machine "Automated teller machine") and front ends for [core banking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Core_banking "Core banking") systems, which led to the launch of the first product, [BASE24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BASE24 "BASE24"), in 1982. BASE24 was coined by a salesman to represent "Baseline Software for 24 hour-per-day system operations".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-3)

BASE24 was expanded over time to service transactions from other channels, such as [POS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/POS_terminal "POS terminal") terminals and bank branch systems. The product portfolio grew to cover functions related to card transactions, such as clearing, settlement and [fraud detection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraud_detection "Fraud detection"). The hardware support for these products was extended to suppliers [IBM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM "IBM"), [HP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hewlett-Packard "Hewlett-Packard"), [Stratus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratus_Technologies "Stratus Technologies") and [Sun Microsystems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Microsystems "Sun Microsystems").

In the 1990s, ACI's product range was expanded to cover [wholesale banking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wholesale_banking "Wholesale banking") payments with software for [ACH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automated_Clearing_House "Automated Clearing House") transactions and [wire transfers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wire_transfer "Wire transfer") leading to the acquisition of IntraNet, Inc. in 1998,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-4) and adding the Money Transfer System product.

Since 1995, ACI has been publicly traded on [NASDAQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASDAQ "NASDAQ"), initially under the name Transaction Systems Architects (TSA), and, since July 2007, under the name ACI Worldwide, Inc. (ACIW).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-ACI-5) Prior to that ACI had periods of ownership by [US West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_West "US West") and Tandem, and as a private company.

### Acquisitions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=ACI_Worldwide&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Acquisitions")]

*   1998: IntraNet, Inc.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-6) was acquired by ACI Worldwide's predecessor Transaction Systems Architects, Inc. IntraNet, Inc. manufactured software systems to facilitate electronic payments.
*   2005: S2 Systems signed an agreement to sell substantially all its assets to Transaction Systems Architects, Inc.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-7)
*   2005: Restructuring of Transaction Systems Architects, Inc. into a highly focused organization, merging ACI, Insession, and IntraNet [[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-9) into one operating unit under the name ACI Worldwide. The name change became official in July 2007.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-ACI-5)
*   2006: P&H Solutions Inc., a provider of a Web-based corporate cash management product, was acquired by ACI Worldwide.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-10)
*   2006: Electronic Payment Systems AG (eps) was acquired.
*   2007: Stratasoft Sdn Bhd was acquired.
*   2007: Visual WEB Solutions Inc.,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-11) a financial banking applications company, was acquired.
*   2009: Euronet Essentis[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-12) was purchased by ACI to expand card issuing and merchant management capabilities[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-13)
*   2011: The acquisition of ISD Corporation was announced[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-14) to broaden the functionality of ACI's payments products for retailers.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-15)
*   2012: [S1 Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S1_Corporation "S1 Corporation") was acquired[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-16) to broaden ACI's suite of payment offerings for financial organizations, processors and retailers.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-18)
*   2012: North Data Uruguay S.A. was acquired.
*   2012: Distra Pty Ltd was acquired.
*   2013: Online Resources Corporation was acquired.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-19)
*   2013: Official Payments Holdings,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-20) a provider of electronic bill payment technology, was acquired. The company processed approximately 20 million payments, totaling over $9 billion annually.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-ACI_Worldwide,_Inc._Form_10-K_Period_Ending_December_31,_2013-21)
*   2013: Profesionales en Transacciones Electronicas S.A. (PTESA) was acquired.
*   2014: An agreement to acquire Retail Decisions (ReD) was announced[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-23) and completed on August 12, 2014.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-24)
*   2015: PAY.ON, which provides white-label hosted payment gateway services, was acquired.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-25)
*   2019: ACI enters agreement to acquire Speedpay,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-26) Western Union's U.S. bill pay business, for $750 million [[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACI_Worldwide#cite_note-27)
*   2019: Walletron was acquired.

# We’ve always been about new ways of working

With the right digital workspace technology, you can be ready for anything

## 16 million cloud users. Thousands of organizations. They all rely on Citrix® to power a better way to work.

When we pioneered remote access, we believed people should be able to work anywhere and in any way they need. Three decades later, that’s even more true than ever.

It’s what drives us to create technology that transcends the constraints of time, place, infrastructure, networks, and devices. And it’s the reason thousands of organizations around the world trust us to keep their apps available, their data safe, and their people productive—wherever and whenever work happens.

**Citrix Systems, Inc.** is an American [multinational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_corporation "Multinational corporation")[cloud computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_computing "Cloud computing") and [virtualization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtualization "Virtualization") technology company that provides server, application and [desktop virtualization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desktop_virtualization "Desktop virtualization"), networking, [software as a service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_as_a_service "Software as a service") (SaaS), and [cloud computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_computing "Cloud computing") technologies. Citrix claims that its products are used by over 400,000 clients worldwide, including 99% of the _Fortune_ 100 and 98% of the [_Fortune_ 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune_500 "Fortune 500").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-2)

In 1989, Citrix was founded in [Richardson, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richardson,_Texas "Richardson, Texas"), by [Ed Iacobucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Iacobucci "Ed Iacobucci"), who served as chairman until his departure in 2000. The company began by developing remote access products for [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft")[operating systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system "Operating system") and licensing [source code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Source_code "Source code") from [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"). Citrix has been partnered with Microsoft throughout its history. By the 1990s, Citrix had become an industry leader in [thin client](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thin_client "Thin client") technology, enabling purpose-built devices to access remote servers and resources. The company launched its first [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") in 1995 and, with few competitors, experienced significant revenue increases between 1995 and 1999.

Citrix acquired Sequoia Software Corp. in 2001 and [ExpertCity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Expertcity "Expertcity"), a provider of remote desktop products, in 2003. This was followed by more than a dozen other acquisitions from 2005 to 2012, which allowed Citrix to expand into additional markets including server and desktop virtualization, cloud computing, [infrastructure as a service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infrastructure_as_a_service "Infrastructure as a service"), and [software as a service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_as_a_service "Software as a service"). In 2014, Citrix acquired Framehawk and used its technology to improve the delivery of virtual desktops and applications over wireless networks. In 2016, as part of a $1.8 billion deal with [LogMeIn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LogMeIn "LogMeIn"), Citrix [spun off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corporate_spin-off "Corporate spin-off") the GoTo product line into a new business entity called GetGo. In 2017, Citrix completed the merger of GetGo with LogMeIn's products.

Citrix is headquartered in [Fort Lauderdale, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Lauderdale,_Florida "Fort Lauderdale, Florida"), with [subsidiary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subsidiary "Subsidiary") operations in California and Massachusetts and additional development centers in Canada, Denmark, Germany, India, and the United Kingdom. In 2021, Citrix generated $3.2 billion in revenue and had 9,700 employees.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-10K2021-1)

After being acquired by [Vista Equity Partners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vista_Equity_Partners "Vista Equity Partners") and Evergreen Coast Capital Corp on September 30, 2022, Citrix merged with [TIBCO Software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TIBCO_Software "TIBCO Software") under the newly formed [Cloud Software Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_Software_Group "Cloud Software Group").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-crn-csg-3) Citrix spun off the re-branded Citrix ADC back into a standalone entity called [NetScaler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NetScaler "NetScaler") under the same parent.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-4)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Citrix_Systems&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Early history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Citrix_Systems&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early history")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Citrix.svg/250px-Citrix.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Citrix.svg)

Original Citrix logo until September 14, 2020

In 1989, Citrix was founded in [Richardson, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richardson,_Texas "Richardson, Texas"), by former [IBM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBM "IBM") developer [Ed Iacobucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Iacobucci "Ed Iacobucci") with $3 million in funding.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-NetIndustries-5) Following the company's initial setup and development, Iacobucci moved the company to his former home in [Coral Springs, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_Springs,_Florida "Coral Springs, Florida").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-NetIndustries-5) The company's first employees were five other engineers from IBM who Iacobucci convinced to join his team. Iacobucci served as chairman of the company, and Roger Roberts became the [CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_executive_officer "Chief executive officer") of Citrix in 1990.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-NetIndustries-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Gibbs99-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Freer97-7) Citrix was originally named Citrus but changed its name after an existing company claimed [trademark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trademark "Trademark") rights.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Heisler-8) The name Citrix is a [portmanteau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portmanteau "Portmanteau") of Citrus and [UNIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNIX "UNIX").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Sarna10-9)

The company's first product was Citrix Multiuser, an extension of [OS/2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OS/2 "OS/2") developed over two years. Citrix licensed the OS/2 [source code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Source_code "Source code") from [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-NetIndustries-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Gibbs99-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Lunan91-10) and developed its own [Independent Computing Architecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_Computing_Architecture "Independent Computing Architecture") (ICA) protocol for Citrix Multiuser.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-11) Multiuser allowed multiple users working on separate computers to remotely access software on a server, even from computers that were not built to run OS/2.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Lunan91-10)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Maney97-12) Three days before the product launched in 1991, Microsoft announced it would be switching from OS/2 to [Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Windows "Microsoft Windows"). This change made Multiuser nearly unusable without significant changes to make it compatible with Windows or [DOS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DOS "DOS"). In 1991, the company discussed closing, but investments from [Intel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intel "Intel"), Microsoft, and [Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kleiner_Perkins_Caufield_&_Byers "Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers") among others allowed the company to work on a new version of Multiuser.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-NetIndustries-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Gibbs99-6)

Multiuser version 2.0 was released in 1992. It was compatible with DOS applications and allowed up to five users.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Salemi92-13) In 1993, Citrix released a new remote applications server, WinView, which could run DOS and Windows applications.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Durlester93-14) By 1994, the company's yearly revenue equaled $10 million.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-NetIndustries-5)

In 1995, the company launched [Citrix WinFrame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix_WinFrame "Citrix WinFrame"), a [multi-user](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-user "Multi-user")[operating system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system "Operating system") based on Microsoft's [Windows NT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windows_NT "Windows NT").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-NetIndustries-5) This new product allowed up to 15 users and was the first [thin client](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thin_client "Thin client") for Windows.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Rigney96-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-PCMag-16)

### Rise in popularity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Citrix_Systems&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Rise in popularity")]

Citrix had its [initial public offering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_public_offering "Initial public offering") in December 1995.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-MiamiHerald12-17) On its first day of trading, the company's share price doubled from $15 to $30.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-NetIndustries-5) During the mid-1990s, Citrix became the leader of its growing industry with very few competitors, and the company's revenues doubled year over year between 1995 and 1999.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Gibbs99-6)

After weeks of discussion, Iacobucci persuaded Microsoft to license Citrix technology for Windows NT Server 4.0, resulting in Windows Terminal Server Edition in 1998.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Gibbs99-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Freer97-7)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-ESJ98-18) This agreement allowed Citrix to keep its position in the marketplace and be NT 4.0 compatible.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Maney97-12) Citrix also earned $75 million and a royalty arrangement valued at approximately $100 million.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Maney97-12)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-MiamiHerald12-17)

Citrix released MetaFrame 1.0 in conjunction with Terminal Server Edition. Due to weaknesses in Microsoft's [Remote Desktop Protocol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remote_Desktop_Protocol "Remote Desktop Protocol") (RDP), Terminal Server Edition worked best with Citrix's ICA protocol which MetaFrame used. This meant that Citrix technology was purchased and installed on most machines that ran Terminal Server Edition.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Freer97-7)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-ESJ98-18)

In 1997, the company opened a new headquarters in [Fort Lauderdale, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Lauderdale,_Florida "Fort Lauderdale, Florida"). It also opened offices in [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"), and [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris") that same year.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-MiamiHerald12-17)

In 1998, [Mark Templeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_B._Templeton "Mark B. Templeton") became the CEO of Citrix after serving as vice president of marketing.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-MiamiHerald12-17) That year, Citrix also licensed its ICA protocol to IBM and Key Tronics.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-NetIndustries-5) In 1999, Citrix licensed its ICA protocol to [Motorola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorola "Motorola") for use in digital wireless handsets.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Gibbs99-6)

During 1999, Citrix's thin-client model became a software trend, and the company's customers increased to 15 million.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-NetIndustries-5) Major clients included [Sears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sears "Sears"), [AT&T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AT&T "AT&T"), and [Chevron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chevron_Corporation "Chevron Corporation").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Freer97-7)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Maney97-12) In 2000, the burst of the [dot-com bubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dot-com_bubble "Dot-com bubble") led to Iacobucci leaving the company and CEO Mark Templeton being demoted to the president and senior executive officer. Templeton was later reinstated in 2001.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-MiamiHerald12-17)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citrix#cite_note-Bryant12-19)

### Expansion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Citrix_Systems&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Expansion")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Citrix_Santa_Clara_HQ_2015.png/330px-Citrix_Santa_Clara_HQ_2015.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Citrix_Santa_Clara_HQ_2015.png)
